Entries.Text: Collision Editor
Collision Editor
This tool is only supported for Elden Ring, Nightreign and Armored Core VI.
Reshape map collision by moving its vertices in the viewport. Edits are previewed until they are committed, which rebuilds the edited collision and writes it into the project.
Collision isn't loaded, so there is nothing to edit. Enable collision loading and load the map again.
Actions
Start or stop editing, and commit or discard the edits.
Start Collision Edit
Shows the cursor on the collision under the mouse, so its vertices can be moved with the keys below.
Stop Collision Edit
Hides the cursor. Edits that haven't been committed are kept, and can be committed or discarded later.
Commit Changes
Rebuilds the edited collision from the moved vertices and writes the collision binders it is in into the project. Can be undone.
Discard Changes
Puts every moved vertex back where it was.
Layer
The collision layer the cursor edits. Only this layer is hit, as the layers lie on top of each other.
High and low collision are the same ground at two levels of detail. Fall protection is a barrier of its own.
{0} collision isn't displayed, so the cursor can't be placed on it.
Display {0} Collision
Displays this collision layer for every collision part.
Linked Layers
Whether the other layer of a part follows the edits, so high and low collision stay on the same ground.
Link High and Low

Moves the vertices of the other layer near the edited vertex by the same amount, and commits both files. The layers don't share vertices, and don't always cover the same ground, so only vertices within the link distance follow. Works whether or not the other layer is displayed.
{0} collision isn't linked to another layer.
{0} collision follows edits to {1} collision.
Link Distance
How close the other layer's vertices must be to the edited vertex to follow it fully. Past it, the radius fades them out.
The distance in world units. In Stormveil, 94% of low vertices lie within 0.5 of the high collision; larger distances may pull in nearby surfaces that aren't the same ground.
Linked: {0}
Linked: none (this part has no other layer that can be edited)
Step
How far each press of the raise or lower key moves the vertex.
The distance in world units, up or down.
Radius
Moves the vertices around the target as well, less the further they are from it.
The distance in world units. 0 moves the target vertex alone.
Cursor Size
The size of the cursor sphere. The vertex marker is a little smaller.
The radius in world units.
Cursor Opacity
How solid the fill inside the cursor's wireframe is. Lower lets the collision under a large cursor show through.
0% leaves the wireframe alone; 100% fills the cursor solid.
Controls
The keys work while the mouse is over the viewport and no mouse button is held, as the mouse buttons fly the camera with the same keys. They can be changed in the keybind settings.
{0}: raise the vertex.
{0}: lower the vertex.
Hold {0}: drag the vertex across the ground at its height.
Cursor
The collision and vertex under the cursor.
Collision is hidden. It must be displayed to be edited.
Start editing to show the cursor.
Collision: {0} ({1})
Vertex {0}: {1}
Move the mouse over a collision to place the cursor.
